stories.headline: King Charles completes US state visit with Congress address, Trump meetings, and Bermuda stopover
stories.summary: King Charles III and Queen Camilla completed a four-day state visit to the United States (April 27-30), including a historic address to a joint session of Congress, a White House state dinner with President Trump, stops in New York and Virginia, and a brief visit to Bermuda. The visit was widely described as a diplomatic triumph aimed at repairing strained UK-US relations, with Trump scrapping Scotch whisky tariffs in its wake.

stories.headline: Golders Green antisemitic stabbing triggers terror threat rise, protest ban debate, and government response
stories.summary: Two Jewish men were stabbed in the Golders Green area of north London in a suspected antisemitic terror attack, prompting the UK to raise its national terrorism threat level to 'severe.' Prime Minister Starmer pledged new protective measures and suggested that some pro-Palestine marches could be banned, sparking a major free speech debate. The cluster also includes Badenoch and others responding to the crisis, investigation of possible Iranian links, and a leaked letter from Netanyahu.

stories.headline: Bank of England holds rates at 3.75% and issues multi-scenario Iran war inflation warnings
stories.summary: The Bank of England's Monetary Policy Committee voted 8-1 to hold interest rates at 3.75% on April 30, citing profound uncertainty from the Iran war and the closure of the Strait of Hormuz. Governor Andrew Bailey set out three economic scenarios, the most severe of which could require 'forceful' rate hikes, while acknowledging policymakers face their 'most difficult combination' of economic conditions.

stories.headline: Labour leadership crisis intensifies ahead of May 7 local elections with Streeting challenge and snap election warning
stories.summary: With Labour expected to suffer heavy losses in May 7 local elections, Health Secretary Wes Streeting secured backing from over 81 Labour MPs to trigger a leadership contest against Starmer. Senior Labour figures warned that removing Starmer risks triggering a snap general election. The crisis is compounded by the ongoing Mandelson appointment scandal, in which Badenoch accused Starmer of misleading Parliament.

stories.headline: Nigel Farage reveals £5m gift from crypto billionaire and firebombing of his home amid scrutiny questions
stories.summary: Nigel Farage disclosed that his home was firebombed in early 2025 and that he received a £5 million personal gift from Thailand-based crypto billionaire Christopher Harborne shortly before announcing his 2024 parliamentary candidacy. Labour and Conservatives accused him of breaking parliamentary rules by not declaring the payment; the Electoral Commission began considering an investigation. Farage then pulled out of a BBC Sunday morning interview, drawing further criticism.

stories.headline: Kemi Badenoch apologises after Conservative social media post used Bloody Sunday footage
stories.summary: A video posted to Kemi Badenoch's social media channels opposing Labour's Northern Ireland Troubles (Legacy) Bill was found to include footage of British soldiers during Bloody Sunday. Badenoch apologised, saying she had not signed off on the video, which was deleted after Northern Irish politicians condemned it as 'disgusting' and 'grossly insulting' to victims' families.

stories.headline: Starmer attends European Political Community summit in Armenia, meets Zelensky, announces UK entry into EU Ukraine loan talks
stories.summary: Prime Minister Starmer travelled to Yerevan, Armenia for the European Political Community summit, meeting Ukrainian President Zelensky bilaterally to discuss peace talks, energy support, and European air defence. The UK announced it would enter talks to join the EU's £78 billion Ukraine loan scheme, in a move described as signalling closer UK-EU ties on defence and security.

stories.headline: Bank of England mortgage data shows lending resilience; housing market hits record high despite Iran war uncertainty
stories.summary: Bank of England data released May 1 showed mortgage approvals rose to a four-month high of 63,531 in March, while consumer credit grew at the fastest annual rate in over two years. Nationwide Building Society separately reported UK house prices jumped to record highs in April, despite economic uncertainty caused by the Iran war.

stories.headline: Rachel Reeves weighs one-year private rent freeze amid Iran war cost-of-living pressures
stories.summary: Reports emerged that Chancellor Rachel Reeves was considering a one-year freeze on private sector rents in England to offset cost-of-living pressures from the Iran war energy crisis. Downing Street quickly distanced itself from the plan, but Reeves declined to deny it publicly, drawing criticism from economists and housing market participants.

The move drew criticism from some who argued it breaches pension fund fiduciary duty.
